governance.decisionForum: King’s Edge Portfolio Board, with the team’s organisational, workforce and professional-practice arrangements governed through the relevant Digital and IT forums.
governance.decisionScope: Material decisions about the team’s remit; the four funded Year One posts, their planning grades, individual costs, final grades, start dates and recurrent implications; whether solution architecture is covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post or separately; the small protected Business Analysis and DevOps/platform allocations; the £90,000 Year One agentic software-development tooling allowance and its final commercial implementation; leadership and decision rights; demand intake and prioritisation; the evidence the first year must generate about team shape and institutional capability; any material increase in first-year Hub scope that would compete with the King’s Edge roadmap; product and delivery practices; interfaces with specialist Digital and IT functions; evidence-based decisions to expand the team; handover criteria; and enduring institutional ownership.
governance.businessAsUsualOwner: TBC – Digital and IT product development capability owner
governance.businessAsUsualOwnershipNote: The capability is expected to sit within Digital and IT. The Year One funded core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit, individually costed posts for the November 2026 to June 2027 planning period: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, approximately £61,000 using a King’s Grade 8 midpoint assumption; 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, approximately £50,000 using Grade 7; 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer, approximately £50,000 using Grade 7; and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer, approximately £42,000 using Grade 6. The estimates include employer pension, employer National Insurance and apprenticeship levy and total approximately £203,000. They replace the previous global staffing holding envelope. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points and start dates. Mark Peace is Product Owner. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Outside the funded core, the working assumption is deliberately lean: approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis during the main discovery period and approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, with up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering post cannot carry that function. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer; specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input is drawn from existing institutional functions when required rather than represented as standing fractional posts. A £90,000 Year One planning allowance for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling is included in the baseline while Digital and IT validates the exact commercial structure and whether shared capacity can reduce the eventual cost. The current overall Year One cash baseline is approximately £358,000. The enduring organisational home, recurrent staffing, professional leadership and relationship to the Digital Student Experience Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2 should be confirmed as the operating model is proven. King’s Edge remains the principal substantive product demand and the September 2027 Hub is a focused first live release.
